reason: Crossing orbits should bring rocky planetesimals into collisions, starting the growth of rocky embryos.
expectation: I expect collisions or an early stage of embryo growth, though some bodies might instead break apart.

alternatives.reason: Breaking the differentiated body could supply metal-rich fragments, but I want to start with the planetesimals.

effect: The collisions produced several growing embryos, so I can now pursue their further growth.
reaction: It is useful to see that multiple embryos grow at once.
reason: Gravitational focusing should help the embryos attract more material and grow.
expectation: I expect a larger rocky embryo, though I don't know which one.

alternatives.reason: Adding rocky planetesimals also seems like a direct way to grow the embryos.

effect: Gravitational focusing produced a larger embryo that can now gather rocky fragments.
reaction: The feedback loop between mass and accretion is a useful connection.
reason: Adding rocky fragments should continue growing the strongly attracting embryo.
expectation: I expect a larger rocky body, though I don't know whether it will become young Earth.

alternatives.reason: Adding planetesimals could grow another embryo, but I want to follow the one already developing.

effect: The rocky fragments formed the proto-Earth; it still needs a source of volatiles.
reaction: It is satisfying to see which embryo becomes Earth.
reason: Breaking the differentiated small world may supply material needed for further growth.
expectation: I expect fragments from its metal core, though I am unsure how they will be used.

alternatives.reason: Growing another embryo also serves a goal, but I want to pursue material for proto-Earth first.

effect: The collision exposed core fragments that can now be added to proto-Earth.
reaction: The connection to iron meteorites is interesting.
reason: Add the metal-rich fragments to continue building proto-Earth.
expectation: I expect proto-Earth to gain metal-rich material, though it may still need water-bearing material.

alternatives.reason: Growing another embryo serves the other goal, but I want to continue the proto-Earth branch.

effect: Proto-Earth has inherited metal and can now acquire water-bearing material.
reaction: The inheritance of material from already differentiated bodies is a useful connection.
reason: Add water-bearing asteroid material to pursue the volatile-bearing young Earth goal.
expectation: I expect a water-bearing proto-Earth, though its water may remain bound in minerals.

alternatives.reason: This could grow the other rocky embryo, but I want to finish the proto-Earth branch first.

effect: The young Earth now carries volatile-bearing material, completing one goal; the other embryo remains to be grown.
reaction: The uncertainty about water sources adds useful context.
reason: This is the only offered combination and should advance the remaining embryo goal.
expectation: I expect the embryos to gather rocky planetesimals and form another larger rocky body.

effect: The remaining combination produced the hypothetical embryo Theia and completed the chapter; its exact properties remain uncertain.
reaction: Theia’s appearance makes me curious about its encounter with Earth.

mostWorthwhile.text: Adding water-bearing asteroid material was worthwhile because it connected planetary growth to water delivery while acknowledging uncertainty about sources and timing.

leastWorthwhile.text: Growing the strongly attracting embryo into proto-Earth was straightforward but less distinctive than the later explanations of inherited material.

surprise.text: A collision exposed metal from a differentiated asteroid’s core, linking the material to some iron meteorites.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt entirely purposeless, although I chose to break the small world before knowing how its fragments would be used.

continue.text: Yes. I would continue to see how Theia’s hypothetical encounter with Earth unfolds, especially given the uncertainty described.
